translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 2
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 2

translations.literal: Basic Annals, Number Two
translations.idiomatic: Annals, Part Two

sentences.zh: 高祖下

translations.literal: The Founder (Part Two)
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, Part Two

sentences.zh: 永定元年冬十月乙亥，高祖即皇帝位于南郊，柴燎告天曰：「皇帝臣霸先，[1]敢用玄牡昭告于皇皇后帝：梁氏以圮剝荐臻，歷運有極，欽若天應，以命于霸先。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongding, on yihai day, the Founder assumed the imperial dignity at the Southern Suburb. With firewood piled for the burnt offering he announced to Heaven: "The Emperor, your subject Baxian, [1] dares to use a black bull to proclaim clearly to the August Empress and August Emperor: The House of Liang, its edifice crumbling, calamity piled upon calamity, its allotted span exhausted—reverently in accord with Heaven's response, the mandate was given to Baxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongding (557), on yihai day, the Founder took the throne at the Southern Suburb. He kindled the firewood offering and addressed Heaven: "Your subject Baxian, now Emperor, [1] ventures to sacrifice a black bull and declare to the August Empress and August Emperor: The Liang dynasty lies in ruins, disaster heaped upon disaster, its mandate spent—yet Heaven's answer has come, and the charge is laid upon Baxian."

sentences.zh: 夫肇有烝民，乃樹司牧，選賢與能，未常厥姓。

translations.literal: From the beginning there have been the multitude of people; therefore rulers were set over them, choosing the worthy and able—never always of one surname.
translations.idiomatic: When the people first arose, rulers were appointed over them; worth and ability, not bloodline alone, decided who would lead.

sentences.zh: 放勛、重華之世，咸無意於受終，當塗、典午之君，雖有心於揖讓，皆以英才處萬乘，高勳御四海，故能大庇黔首，光宅區縣。

translations.literal: In the ages of Fangxun and Chonghua, both were without intent to receive the end; the lords of Dangtu and Dianwu, though they had mind for yielding, all alike placed men of outstanding talent upon the ten-thousand chariots, with high merit steering the four seas—therefore they could greatly shelter the black-haired people and brightly settle the districts and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun took the throne without seeking it; the rulers of Wei and Jin, though they spoke of abdication, still set men of rare talent upon the throne and men of towering merit at the helm of the realm—thus they sheltered the people and brought order to the land.

sentences.zh: 有梁末運，仍葉遘屯，獯醜憑陵，久移神器，承聖在外，非能祀夏，天未悔禍，復罹寇逆，嫡嗣廢黜，宗枝僭詐，天地蕩覆，紀綱泯絕。

translations.literal: In the final fortune of Liang, misfortune still followed misfortune; savage foes leaned upon the borders, and for long the sacred vessel shifted. Emperor Chengsheng was abroad and could not sacrifice to Xia; Heaven had not yet repented the calamity, and again they suffered bandit invasions. The legitimate heir was deposed and discarded; collateral branches usurped by fraud. Heaven and earth were overturned; statutes and norms were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's last days disaster followed disaster. Barbarian armies trampled the borders and the imperial regalia passed from hand to hand. Emperor Chengsheng languished in exile, unable to keep the altars of state; Heaven had not yet lifted the scourge, and rebels struck again. The rightful heir was cast aside; kinsmen seized power by deceit. Heaven and earth were overturned; law and order perished.

sentences.zh: 霸先爰初投袂，大拯橫流，重舉義兵，實戡多難，廢王立帝，寔有厥功，安國定社，用盡其力。

translations.literal: Baxian at the first cast aside his sleeve and greatly rescued the crosscurrent; again he raised the righteous army and truly conquered many hardships; deposing a king and establishing an emperor, he truly had merit therein; settling the state and fixing the altars, he exhausted his strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder first flung aside his robe and plunged into the flood to save the realm; again he raised righteous armies and truly cut through countless perils. He deposed one ruler and set up another—merit undeniable—and gave all his strength to secure the nation and its altars.

sentences.zh: 是謂小康，方期大道。

translations.literal: This is called modest prosperity; one looks toward the Great Way.
translations.idiomatic: This was modest order; the Great Way still lay ahead.

sentences.zh: 既而煙雲表色，日月呈瑞，緯聚東井，龍見譙邦，除舊布新，既彰玄象，遷虞事夏，且協謳訟，[2]九域八荒，同布衷款，百神群祀，皆有誠願。

translations.literal: Thereafter clouds and mist showed color; sun and moon presented omens; constellations gathered at the Eastern Well; a dragon appeared in the Qiao region. Removing the old and spreading the new, the dark signs were already manifest; shifting from Yu and serving Xia, and moreover matching the songs of praise, [2] the nine domains and eight wilds alike spread forth sincere petitions; the hundred spirits and assembled sacrifices all had sincere wish.
translations.idiomatic: Then clouds and mist took auspicious hues; sun and moon showed signs; stars clustered at the Eastern Well; a dragon was seen in Qiao. The old order gave way to the new, and Heaven's signs were plain; as in the transfer from Shun to Yu, the people's acclaim agreed. [2] Within the nine provinces and beyond the eight directions, loyal petitions poured in; every spirit and rite was offered in earnest devotion.

sentences.zh: 梁帝高謝萬邦，授以大寶，霸先自惟菲薄，讓德不嗣，至于再三，辭弗獲許。

translations.literal: The Liang Emperor, with lofty yielding, surrendered the myriad states and conferred the great treasure. Baxian, considering himself slight, yielded virtue and would not succeed; even to a third time, his refusal could not obtain consent.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor abdicated with lofty grace and handed over the great seal. The Founder, judging himself unworthy, declined again and again; a third time he refused, yet consent was denied him.

sentences.zh: 僉以百姓須主，萬機難曠，皇靈眷命，非可謙拒。

translations.literal: All said that the hundred surnames needed a lord and the myriad affairs could not be left vacant; the imperial numen favored the mandate—it could not be modestly refused.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed that the people needed a ruler and the myriad affairs of state could not stand idle; Heaven's favor rested on him—humility was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 畏天之威，用膺嘉祚，永言夙志，能無慚德。

translations.literal: In awe of Heaven's majesty, he received the fine fortune; ever mindful of long-held resolve, how could he be without shame in virtue?
translations.idiomatic: In awe of Heaven's majesty he accepted the glorious mandate; yet remembering his lifelong modesty, how could he be free of shame?

sentences.zh: 敬簡元辰，升壇受禪，告類上帝，用答民心，永保于我有陳。

translations.literal: Reverently selecting the first day, he ascended the altar and received the abdication, announcing his category to the August Lord, to answer the people's heart—forever to preserve our Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He reverently chose the auspicious day, ascended the altar, and received the abdication, reporting to the Supreme Lord to answer the people's hearts—may Chen endure forever.

sentences.zh: 惟明靈是饗！

translations.literal: May the bright spirits partake!
translations.idiomatic: May the bright spirits accept this offering!

sentences.zh: 」先是氛霧，晝夜晦冥，至于是日，景氣清晏，識者知有天道焉。

translations.literal: " Earlier there had been miasma and fog; day and night were dim and dark. On this day the atmosphere was clear and calm; those who knew recognized that Heaven's Way was at work.
translations.idiomatic: " Before this, miasma and fog had shrouded the land in unbroken gloom. On that day the air cleared and grew serene; the discerning knew Heaven's Way was at work.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，輿駕還宮，臨太極前殿。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the imperial carriage returned to the palace and proceeded to the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, the imperial carriage returned to the palace and halted before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「五德更運，帝王所以御天，三正相因，夏、殷所以宰世，雖色分辭翰，時異文質，揖讓征伐，迄用參差，而育德振民，義歸一揆。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Five Virtues rotate in succession—therefore emperors and kings rule Heaven. The Three Rectifications follow one another—therefore Xia and Yin govern the age. Though colors differed in written edicts and times differed in pattern and substance, yielding and warfare, expeditions and punishments, were used in varying measure; yet to nurture virtue and stir the people, the principle returns to one standard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The Five Virtues succeed one another, and thus emperors and kings hold Heaven's mandate. The Three Rectifications follow in turn, and thus Xia and Yin governed the world. Though ritual color and written style changed with the age, and abdication gave way to conquest as times required, the aim was always one: to nurture virtue and lift up the people."

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，時屬艱危，國步屢屯，天維三絕，肆勤先后，拯厥橫流，藉將帥之功，兼猛士之力，一匡天下，再造黔黎。

translations.literal: We, slight and dim, at the time met with hardship and peril; the state's steps repeatedly met distress; Heaven's cords thrice snapped. Diligently we toiled for our forebears and rescued that crosscurrent, relying on our generals' merit and joining the fierce warriors' strength—once to set the realm right and twice to remake the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: "We, unworthy and obscure, came to power in grievous times. The throne stumbled again and again; Heaven's bonds were thrice severed. We labored for our ancestors' sake to stem the flood, leaning on our commanders' deeds and our warriors' might—once to restore the realm and again to remake the people."

sentences.zh: 梁氏以天祿永終，歷數攸在，遵與能之典，集大命于朕躬。

translations.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing ended forever, its sequence where it belonged, followed the canon of yielding to the able and gathered the great mandate upon Our person.
translations.idiomatic: The House of Liang, its heavenly mandate exhausted, its turn complete, followed the ancient canon of yielding to the worthy and laid the great charge upon Our person."

sentences.zh: 顧惟菲德，辭不獲亮，式從天睠，俯協民心，受終文祖，升禋上帝，繼跡百王，君臨萬宇，若涉川水，罔知攸濟。

translations.literal: Looking back on Our slight virtue, Our refusal could not obtain clarity; following Heaven's favor, We bow to match the people's heart, receiving the end from the Culture Ancestor, ascending to offer to the August Lord, continuing the traces of the hundred kings, ruling over the ten thousand realms—like crossing river water, We know not where to ford.
translations.idiomatic: "Reflecting on Our meager worth, We could not refuse with honor; bowing to Heaven's favor and the people's will, We received the mandate from the culture-ancestor, ascended to worship the Supreme Lord, and took up the hundred kings' legacy to rule the world—like a man fording a river without knowing the far shore."

sentences.zh: 寶業初建，皇祚惟新，思俾惠澤，覃被億兆。

translations.literal: The precious enterprise newly founded, the imperial fortune newly renewed—We think to extend gracious favor and spread it over the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: "Our dynasty is newly founded, Our fortune freshly renewed; We mean to spread gracious bounty to the hundred millions."

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下，改梁太平二年為永定元年。

translations.literal: Let there be a great amnesty for all under Heaven; change Liang's second year of Taiping to the first year of Yongding.
translations.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm, and let Liang's second year of Taiping be renamed the first year of Yongding."

sentences.zh: 賜民爵二級，文武二等。

translations.literal: Bestow on the people two ranks of nobility; on civil and military officials, two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Grant the people two ranks of nobility and civil and military officials two grades of promotion."

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者人穀五斛。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves—five hu of grain per person.
translations.idiomatic: Give five hu of grain to each widower, widow, orphan, or solitary who cannot support himself."

sentences.zh: 逋租宿債，皆勿復收。

translations.literal: Overdue rents and old debts—all shall not again be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Overdue rents and old debts shall not be collected again."

sentences.zh: 其有犯鄉里清議贓汙淫盜者，皆洗除先注，與之更始。

translations.literal: Those who have violated village pure criticism, corruption, lewdness, or theft—all shall wash away prior entries and be given a fresh start.
translations.idiomatic: Those guilty of village scandal, corruption, debauchery, or theft shall have prior records erased and begin anew."

sentences.zh: 長徒敕繫，特皆原之。

translations.literal: Long-term convicts under edict imprisonment—all are specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Long-term prisoners held under imperial order are specially pardoned."

sentences.zh: 亡官失爵，禁錮奪勞，一依舊典。

translations.literal: Loss of office and forfeiture of rank, prohibition and deprivation of honors—all follow the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Loss of office, forfeiture of rank, and penalties of disgrace and barred honors shall follow the former statutes."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「禮陳杞、宋，詩詠二客，弗臣之重，歷代斯敦。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "The Rites set forth Qi and Song; the Odes sing of the two guests—the weight of not treating them as subjects, each generation has honored this.
translations.idiomatic: A second edict read: "The Rites enshrine the houses of Qi and Song; the Odes praise the two guest-lords—the ancient honor of not treating them as mere subjects, which every age has upheld.

sentences.zh: 梁氏欽若人祇，憲章在昔，濟河沈璧，高謝萬邦，茅賦所加，宜遵舊典。

translations.literal: The House of Liang, reverently in accord with the people's lord, took its model from the past; crossing the river and sinking the jade disk, with lofty yielding it surrendered the myriad states—the thatch tribute conferred should follow the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: The House of Liang, reverent toward Heaven and the people, took its model from antiquity; crossing the river and casting the jade disk into the stream, it abdicated with lofty grace and surrendered the realm. The tribute of thatch we now confer shall follow the old precedent."

sentences.zh: 其以江陰郡奉梁主為江陰王，行梁正朔，車旗服色，一依前準，宮館資待，務盡優隆。

translations.literal: Let Jiangyin commandery be used to enfeoff the Liang ruler as King of Jiangyin, observing Liang's calendar, with chariots, banners, and dress all according to former standards; palace quarters and stipends shall be maintained with full generous elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Let Jiangyin commandery support the Liang ruler as King of Jiangyin, keeping Liang's calendar, with chariots, banners, and regalia as before; his palaces and stipends shall be maintained in full honor."

sentences.zh: 」又詔梁皇太后為江陰國太妃，皇后為江陰國妃。

translations.literal: " Another edict made the Liang Empress Dowager Grand Princess of the State of Jiangyin and the Empress Consort Princess of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict named the Liang empress dowager Grand Princess of Jiangyin and the empress consort Princess of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 又詔百司依位攝職。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered the hundred offices to assume their duties according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered all offices to resume their duties according to rank.

sentences.zh: 景子，輿駕幸鍾山祠蔣帝廟。

translations.literal: On jingzi day the imperial carriage visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: On jingzi day the emperor visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，輿駕幸華林園，親覽詞訟，臨赦囚徒。

translations.literal: On wuyin day the imperial carriage visited the Hualin Park, personally reviewing lawsuits and pardoning prisoners on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day the emperor went to Hualin Park, personally heard lawsuits, and pardoned prisoners on the spot.

sentences.zh: 己卯，分遣大使宣勞四方，下璽書敕州郡曰：「夫四王革代，商、周所以應天，五勝相推，軒、羲所以當運。

translations.literal: On jimao day he dispatched great envoys to proclaim comfort to the four quarters and sent down imperial-seal letters instructing the provinces and commanderies, saying: "The four kings changed the age—Shang and Zhou thereby answered Heaven; the Five Victories succeeded one another—Xuan and Xi thereby met their fortune.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day he sent great envoys to proclaim comfort to the four quarters, issuing sealed letters of instruction to the provinces and commanderies: "The four kings changed the age—Shang and Zhou thus answered Heaven; the Five Agents succeeded one another—Xuan and Xi thus met their destined turn."

sentences.zh: 梁德不造，喪亂積年，東夏崩騰，西都蕩覆。

translations.literal: Liang's virtue was unmade; mourning and disorder piled up for years. The eastern domains collapsed in turmoil; the western capital was swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's mandate failed; mourning and chaos lasted for years. The east erupted in rebellion; the western capital was overrun."

sentences.zh: 蕭勃干紀，非唯趙倫，侯景滔天，踰於劉載。

translations.literal: Xiao Bo defied the statutes—he was not merely Zhao Lun. Hou Jing reached to Heaven—he surpassed Liu Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bo rebelled against the throne—his crime outdid Zhao Lun's. Hou Jing's outrage touched Heaven—it exceeded Liu Zai's."

sentences.zh: 貞陽反篡，賊約連兵，江左累屬於鮮卑，金陵久非於梁國。

translations.literal: Zhenyang turned traitor and usurped; the bandits' pact linked armies. The lands east of the Yangtze long belonged to the Xianbei; Jinling for long was no longer the land of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyang seized the throne by treachery; rebels joined forces in league. The lands east of the Yangtze fell under Xianbei rule; Jinling for long was no longer Liang's."

sentences.zh: 有自氤氳混沌之世，[3]龍圖鳳紀之前，東漢興平之初，西朝永嘉之亂，天下分崩，未有若於梁朝者也。

translations.literal: From the age of swirling chaos since primordial mist, [3] before the dragon chart and phoenix record, from the beginning of Eastern Han's Xingping, through Western Jin's Yongjia turmoil—the realm split apart, never as in the Liang dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of primordial chaos, [3] before the dragon chart and phoenix annals, from Eastern Han's Xingping through Western Jin's Yongjia disaster—the realm has fractured, but never as ruinously as under Liang."

sentences.zh: 朕以虛薄，屬當興運，自昔登庸，首清諸越，徐門浪泊，靡不征行，浮海乘山，所在戡定。

translations.literal: We, empty and slight, met with the rising fortune. From old upon taking office We first cleared the Yue regions; Xumen and Langbo—none went unmarched upon. Crossing seas and scaling mountains, wherever We went was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: "We, unworthy and slight, came to power at a time of renewal. From our first rise we cleared the Yue lands; at Xumen and Langbo we left no foe unbeaten. Crossing seas and climbing mountains, we pacified wherever we marched."

sentences.zh: 冒愬風塵，騁馳師旅，六延梁祀，十翦彊寇，豈曰人謀，皆由天啟。

translations.literal: Braving complaint and wind-blown dust, galloping with the army—we extended Liang's sacrifices six times and cut down powerful bandits tenfold. How could one call it human counsel alone? All was opened by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We braved dust and hardship and drove our armies hard—six times we prolonged Liang's rites, ten times we struck down mighty rebels. This was not human planning alone; Heaven opened the way."

sentences.zh: 梁氏以天祿斯改，期運永終，欽若唐、虞，推其鼎玉，朕東西退讓，拜手陳辭，避舜子於箕山之陽，求支伯於滄洲之野，而公卿敦逼，率土翹惶，天命難稽，遂享嘉祚。

translations.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing now changed, its allotted span ended forever—reverently in accord with Tang and Yu, they pushed forth their tripod and jade. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and spoke our plea, avoiding Shun's son on the sunny slope of Mount Ji, seeking Zhibo on the wilds of Cangzhou—but the dukes and ministers pressed urgently; the whole land looked up in alarm. Heaven's mandate could not be delayed; thus We received the fine fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The House of Liang, its mandate spent, its turn complete—like Tang and Yu they offered up the regalia. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and pleaded our case, hiding like Shun's son on Mount Ji's sunny slope, seeking Zhibo on Cangzhou's wilds—but ministers pressed us and the realm looked up in dread. Heaven's mandate would not wait; thus We received the glorious throne."

sentences.zh: 今月乙亥，升禮太壇，言念遷

translations.literal: This month on yihai We ascended the rites at the Great Altar, thinking of the transfer
translations.idiomatic: This month, on yihai, We performed the rites at the Great Altar, mindful of the transfer

translations.literal: (jiong)
translations.idiomatic: (jiong)

sentences.zh: 〔桐〕，[4]但有慚德。

translations.literal: [alternate: tong], [4] yet We have shame in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: [alternate reading: tong], [4] yet We are ashamed of Our meager worth.

sentences.zh: 自梁氏將末，頻月亢陽，火運斯終，秋霖奄降。

translations.literal: From the time Liang neared its end, for months the sun stood drought-strong; the fire cycle ended, and autumn rains suddenly fell.
translations.idiomatic: As Liang neared its end, drought blazed for months; the fire cycle closed, and autumn rains burst forth.

sentences.zh: 翌日成禮，圓丘宿設，埃雲晚霽，星象夜張。

translations.literal: The next day the rites were completed; the round mound was set overnight. Dust clouds cleared at evening; the stars spread at night.
translations.idiomatic: On the morrow the rites were complete. The round altar had been prepared overnight; evening dust clouds cleared and the stars shone forth.

sentences.zh: 朝景重輪，泫三危之膏露，晨光合璧，帶五色之卿雲。

translations.literal: The morning scene showed a doubled sun-disk; it dripped the fat dew of Mount Sanwei. The morning light joined jade disks; it bore five-colored minister-clouds.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the sun showed a double halo, dripping the sacred dew of Mount Sanwei; morning light joined like paired jades, trailing five-colored auspicious clouds.

sentences.zh: 顧惟寡薄，彌慚休祉，昧旦丕顯，方思至治。

translations.literal: Looking back on Our slightness, We are the more ashamed of this fine blessing. From cockcrow We strive for greatness; We now think of utmost governance.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on Our slight worth, We are the more ashamed of such blessing. From cockcrow We labor for good government and now ponder how best to rule.

sentences.zh: 卿等擁旄方岳，相任股肱，剖符名守，[5]方寄恤隱。

translations.literal: You, bearing halberds in the border provinces, share in responsibility as Our arms and thighs; with divided tallies as famed administrators, [5] We entrust you with compassionate care for the people.
translations.idiomatic: You who bear command in the provinces are Our arms and thighs; you who hold the tallies as governors [5] are charged with pity for the people.

sentences.zh: 王曆惟新，念有欣慶，想深求民瘼，務在廉平，愛惠以撫孤貧，威刑以御彊猾。

translations.literal: The imperial calendar is newly renewed—think of the people's joy. Deeply seek the people's afflictions; strive for integrity and fairness. Cherish and favor to comfort the orphaned and poor; authority and punishment to restrain the violent and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar is newly renewed—share in the people's joy. Probe deeply for their hardships; keep government honest and fair. Show kindness to orphans and the poor; use stern law against the violent and cunning.

sentences.zh: 若有萑蒲之盜，[6]或犯戎商，山谷之酋，擅彊幽險，皆從肆赦，咸使知聞。

translations.literal: If there are reed-marsh bandits, [6] or offenders against military law, chieftains of mountain valleys who tyrannize in hidden defiles—all are within the general pardon; let all know this.
translations.idiomatic: Reed-marsh bandits [6] who break martial law, mountain chiefs who lord over hidden passes—all are included in the amnesty; make this known everywhere.

sentences.zh: 如或迷途，俾在無貸。

translations.literal: If any still lose the way, they shall have no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Those who still stray from the path shall receive no mercy.

sentences.zh: 今遣使人具宣往旨，念思善政，副此虛懷。」

translations.literal: Now We send envoys to proclaim fully the former intent. Think on good government and answer this empty heart."
translations.idiomatic: We now send envoys to proclaim Our intent in full. Devise good government and answer Our earnest hope."

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔出佛牙於杜姥宅，集四部設無遮大會，高祖親出闕前禮拜。

translations.literal: On gengchen day an edict ordered the Buddha's tooth brought forth from the Du family's old residence; the four assemblies were gathered for an unbounded great assembly, and the Founder personally came forth before the palace gate to bow in worship.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day an edict brought the Buddha's tooth forth from the Du family's old residence. The four assemblies were gathered for a boundless great assembly, and the Founder came in person before the palace gate to bow in worship.

sentences.zh: 初，齊故僧統法獻於烏纏國得之，常在定林上寺，梁天監末，為攝山慶雲寺沙門慧興保藏，慧興將終，以屬弟慧志，承聖末，慧志密送于高祖，至是乃出。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qi former Buddhist superintendent Fazian had obtained it in the Wuchan state; it had long been at Dinglin Upper Monastery. In the last years of Liang's Tianjian era, Shramana Huixing of Sheshan Qingyun Monastery kept it in safekeeping. When Huixing was near death he entrusted it to his younger brother Huizhi. At the end of the Chengsheng era Huizhi secretly sent it to the Founder; only now was it brought forth.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Fazian, former Buddhist superintendent of Qi, had obtained it in Wuchan; it had remained at Dinglin Upper Monastery. In the last years of Liang's Tianjian reign the monk Huixing of Qingyun Monastery on She Mountain kept it safe. On his deathbed Huixing entrusted it to his brother Huizhi. At the end of the Chengsheng era Huizhi secretly sent it to the Founder; only now was it displayed.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，追尊皇考曰景皇帝，廟號太祖；

translations.literal: On xinsi day the Founder's late father was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, temple name Taizu;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the Founder's late father was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, with temple name Taizu;

sentences.zh: 皇妣董太夫人曰安皇后。

translations.literal: the Founder's late mother Lady Dong as Empress An.
translations.idiomatic: and the Founder's late mother, Lady Dong, as Empress An.

sentences.zh: 追謚前夫人錢氏號為昭皇后，世子克為孝懷太子。

translations.literal: The former primary consort, the Qian clan, was given posthumous title Empress Zhao; the heir Ke was titled Filial and Cherishing Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The former primary consort of the Qian clan was posthumously titled Empress Zhao; the heir Ke was named Filial and Cherishing Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 立夫人章氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang was established as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 癸未，尊景帝陵曰瑞陵，昭皇后陵曰嘉陵，依梁初園陵故事。

translations.literal: On guiwei day Emperor Jing's tomb was honored as Ruiling and Empress Zhao's tomb as Jialing, following Liang's early garden-tomb precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Emperor Jing's tomb was styled Ruiling and Empress Zhao's Jialing, following Liang's early garden-tomb precedent.

sentences.zh: 立刪定郎，治定律令。

translations.literal: Revision and codification officers were established to compile and fix laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Officers for revision and codification were appointed to compile laws and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 戊子，遷景皇帝神主祔于太廟。

translations.literal: On wuzi day the spirit tablet of Emperor Jing was moved to take its place in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day the spirit tablet of Emperor Jing was enshrined in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以中權將軍、開府儀同三司、丹陽尹王沖為左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On xinmao day the Central Authority General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Danyang Intendant Wang Chong was made Left Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Wang Chong, central authority general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and Danyang intendant, was made left grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，追贈皇兄梁故散騎常侍、平北將軍、兗州刺史[7]長城縣公道譚驃騎大將軍、太尉，封始興郡王；

translations.literal: On guisi day the Founder's elder brother, Liang former Scattered Cavalry Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, and Yanzhou Inspector [7] Duke Daotan of Changcheng county, was posthumously honored as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as King of Shixing;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day the Founder's elder brother, the late Liang scattered-cavalry palace attendant, general who pacifies the north, and Yanzhou inspector [7] Duke Daotan of Changcheng county, was posthumously made grand general of agile cavalry and grand tutor and enfeoffed as King of Shixing;

sentences.zh: 弟梁故侍中、驃騎將軍、南徐州刺史武康縣侯[8]休先車騎大將軍、司徒，封南康郡王。

translations.literal: his younger brother, Liang former Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and South Xuzhou Inspector Marquis Xiuxian of Wukang county [8] was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of Education and enfeoffed as King of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother, the late Liang palace attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and South Xuzhou inspector [8] Marquis Xiuxian of Wukang county, was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and minister of education and enfeoffed as King of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 是月，西討都督周文育、侯安都於郢州敗績，囚于王琳。

translations.literal: That month, Western Campaign Commander-in-Chief Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu suffered defeat at Yingzhou and were imprisoned by Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: That month the western campaign commander Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu were defeated at Yingzhou and taken prisoner by Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 十一月景申，詔曰：「東都齊國，義乃親賢，西漢城陽，事兼功烈。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jingshen day, an edict said: "The eastern capital's State of Qi honored kinship as worthy; Western Han's Prince of Chengyang combined merit with affection.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jingshen day, an edict declared: "The eastern capital honored Qi for kinship and worth together; Western Han's Prince of Chengyang joined merit with family bond."

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、使持節、都督會稽等十郡諸軍事、宣毅將軍、會稽太守長城縣侯蒨，學尚清優，神宇凝正，文參禮樂，武定妖氛，心力謀猷，為家治國，擁旄作守，期月有成，辟彼關河，[9]功踰蕭、寇，萑蒲之盜，自反耕農，篁竹之豪，用稟聲朔。

translations.literal: Scattered Cavalry Palace Attendant, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Kuaiji and ten commanderies' military affairs, General Who Proclaims Martial Valor, and Kuaiji Administrator Marquis Qian of Changcheng county—his learning esteems pure refinement; his spirit and bearing are concentrated and correct. In letters he joins ritual and music; in arms he settles demonic vapors. With heart-strength and stratagems he governs the family and orders the state. Bearing the halberd as defender, within a month he had achievement. Opening those border passes, [9] his merit surpassed Xiao and Kou; reed-marsh bandits returned of themselves to farming; bamboo-grove magnates submitted to Our sound and calendar.
translations.idiomatic: "Scattered-cavalry palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Kuaiji and ten commanderies, general who proclaims martial valor, and Kuaiji administrator Marquis Qian of Changcheng—his learning is pure and refined, his bearing grave and correct. In civil affairs he upholds ritual and music; in war he quells rebellion. With heart and stratagem he has ordered home and state alike. As territorial defender, within a month he brought order. On the frontier passes [9] his merit outdid Xiao Can and Kou Xun; marsh bandits returned to the plow; mountain lords accepted Our calendar."

sentences.zh: 朕以虛寡，屬當興運，提彼三尺，賓于四門，王業艱難，賴乎此子，宜隆上爵，稱是元功。

translations.literal: We, empty and few, met the rising fortune. Taking up the three-foot [sword] We received guests at the four gates. The royal enterprise was hard and perilous—we rely on this son. Let him receive lofty rank fitting this primary merit.
translations.idiomatic: "We, unworthy and alone, came to power in a time of renewal. With sword in hand We opened the four gates to talent. The founding of the dynasty was arduous—we lean on this son. Let him receive exalted rank worthy of his foremost merit."

sentences.zh: 可封臨川郡王，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He may be enfeoffed as King of Linchuan, fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be enfeoffed as King of Linchuan with a fief of two thousand households."

sentences.zh: 兄子梁中書侍郎頊襲封始興王，弟子梁中書侍郎曇朗襲封南康王，禮秩一同正王。

translations.literal: The elder brother's son, Liang Central Secretariat Gentleman Xu, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Shixing; the younger brother's son, Liang Central Secretariat Gentleman Tanlang, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Nankang—their ritual ranks the same as full kings.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Xu, former Liang gentleman of the central secretariat, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Shixing; his younger brother's son Tanlang, former Liang gentleman of the central secretariat, inherited as King of Nankang—their ritual standing equal to that of reigning kings.

sentences.zh: 」己亥，甘露降于鍾山松林，彌滿巖谷。

translations.literal: On jihai day sweet dew fell in the pine forest of Zhongshan, filling the cliffs and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day sweet dew fell in the pine forest of Zhongshan until cliffs and valleys were full.

sentences.zh: 庚子，開善寺沙門採之以獻，敕頒賜群臣。

translations.literal: On gengzi day a monk of Kaishan Monastery gathered it and presented it; an edict ordered it distributed to the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day a monk of Kaishan Monastery gathered it and presented it; an edict ordered it distributed among the ministers.

sentences.zh: 景辰，以鎮西將軍、南豫州刺史徐度為鎮右將軍、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On jingchen day the General Who Pacifies the West and South Yuzhou Inspector Xu Du was made General Who Pacifies the Right and Commander of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: On jingchen day Xu Du, general who pacifies the west and South Yuzhou inspector, was made general who pacifies the right and commander of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 庚申，京師大火。

translations.literal: On gengshen day a great fire broke out in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day a great fire broke out in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚辰，皇后謁太廟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, the Empress visited the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, the empress visited the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月乙未，詔曰：「夫設官分職，因事重輕，羽儀車馬，隨時隆替，晉之五校，鳴笳啟途，漢之九卿，傳呼並迾，虞官夏禮，豈曰同科，殷朴周文，固無恆格。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on yiwei day, an edict said: "Setting offices and dividing duties follows the weight of affairs; feathered banners and chariots and horses rise and fall with the times. Jin's Five Commandants sounded the reed-whistle to open the road; Han's Nine Ministers had runners call out together as they passed—rites of Yu and Xia, how could they be one standard? Yin simplicity and Zhou pattern surely have no fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year, on yiwei day of the first month, an edict declared: "Offices and duties are weighed by the business at hand; ceremonial escorts rise and fall with the age. Jin's Five Commandants sounded the reed-pipe to clear the road; Han's nine ministers had heralds cry out as they passed—Yu and Xia rites were not one model; Yin austerity and Zhou ornament had no fixed pattern."

sentences.zh: 朕膺茲寶歷，代是天工，留念官方，庶允時衷。

translations.literal: We have received this precious succession, replacing Heaven's work; We keep in mind the official ranks, that they may match the time's core.
translations.idiomatic: "We have received the sacred succession and take up Heaven's task; We mean to restore official ranks to suit the present need."

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，左右驍騎領朱衣直閤，並給儀從，北徐州刺史

translations.literal: In Liang's Tianjian era, the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry led the Vermilion-Robed Direct Attendants and were both given ceremonial escorts. The North Xuzhou Inspector
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang's Tianjian reign, the left and right valiant cavalry led the vermilion-robed direct attendants and were both granted ceremonial escorts. The North Xuzhou inspector

translations.idiomatic: (chang)

sentences.zh: 〔昌〕義之

translations.literal: [alternate: chang] Yizhi
translations.idiomatic: [alternate reading: chang] Yizhi

translations.idiomatic: (chu)

sentences.zh: 首為此職。

translations.literal: was the first to hold this office.
translations.idiomatic: was the first to hold this office.

sentences.zh: [10]亂離歲久，朝典不存，後生年少，希聞舊則。

translations.literal: [10] Disorder and separation for years on end—the court canon did not survive. The young of later generations scarcely heard the old rules.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Years of chaos have effaced the court's precedents; the young scarcely know the old rules.

sentences.zh: 今去左右驍騎，宜通文武，文官則用腹心，武官則用功臣，所給儀從，同太子二衛率。

translations.literal: Now abolishing the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry, they should unite civil and military; for civil officials use trusted intimates, for military officials use meritorious ministers. The ceremonial escort granted shall match the crown prince's two guard commanders.
translations.idiomatic: We now abolish the left and right valiant cavalry and make the post serve both civil and military ranks—civil officials drawn from trusted intimates, military from meritorious commanders—with escorts equal to the crown prince's two guard commanders.

sentences.zh: 此外眾官，尚書詳為條制。

translations.literal: For other offices as well, the Masters of Writing shall draw up detailed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: For all other offices the Masters of Writing shall draft detailed regulations."

sentences.zh: 」車騎將軍、開府儀同三司侯瑱進位司空，中權將軍、開府儀同三司、新除左光祿大夫王沖為太子少傅。

translations.literal: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Hou Tian advanced in rank to Minister of Works; Central Authority General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and newly appointed Left Grand Master of the Palace Wang Chong became Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian, grand general of chariots and cavalry and grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, was promoted to minister of works; Wang Chong, central authority general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and newly appointed left grand master of the palace, became junior tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍徐世譜為護軍將軍，南兗州刺史吳明徹進號安南將軍，衡州刺史歐陽頠進號鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Xu Shipu became General Who Protects the Army; South Yanzhou Inspector Wu Mingche advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South; Hengzhou Inspector Ouyang Yi advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shipu, left guard general, became general who protects the army; Wu Mingche, South Yanzhou inspector, was promoted to general who pacifies the south; Ouyang Yi, Hengzhou inspector, was promoted to general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，輿駕親祠南郊。

translations.literal: On xinchou day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the emperor sacrificed in person at the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕受命君臨，初移星琯，孟陬嘉月，備禮泰壇，景候昭華，人祗允慶，思令億兆，咸與惟新。

translations.literal: An edict said: "We received the mandate and rule as lord; the stars have newly shifted. In the first month of auspicious spring the full rites were performed at the Great Altar. The seasonal signs were bright and splendid; the people's lord approved the celebration. We think to make the hundred millions all share in renewal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "We received the mandate and now rule the realm; the calendar has newly turned. In the auspicious first month We completed the rites at the Great Altar. The seasons showed bright signs; Heaven and the people rejoiced together. We mean for the hundred millions to share in this renewal."

sentences.zh: 且往代祅氛，于今猶梗，軍機未息，徵賦咸繁，事不獲已，久知下弊，言念黔黎，無忘寢食。

translations.literal: Moreover, demonic vapors of former ages still obstruct today; military affairs have not ceased; levies and corvée are all heavy. Affairs could not be otherwise—we have long known the harm below. Speaking of the black-haired people, We cannot forget them even in sleep.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the evil vapors of former days still linger; armies have not rested; levies remain heavy. Necessity alone drove this—we have long known the people's hardship. When We think of the common folk, We cannot sleep in peace."

sentences.zh: 夫罪無輕重，已發覺未發覺，在今昧爽以前，皆赦除之。

translations.literal: Crimes, whether light or heavy, already discovered or not yet discovered—before dawn today all are pardoned and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes light or heavy, discovered or not—before dawn today all are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 西寇自王琳以下，並許返迷，一無所問。

translations.literal: Western bandits from Wang Lin downward—all are permitted to return from error; nothing shall be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Western rebels from Wang Lin downward may return to the fold without question.

sentences.zh: 近所募義軍，本擬西寇，並宜解遣，留家附業。

translations.literal: Recently recruited righteous armies, originally intended for the western bandits, should all be dismissed and sent home to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteer armies lately raised against the western foe shall be disbanded and sent home to their fields.

sentences.zh: 晚訂軍資未送者並停，元年軍糧逋餘者原其半。

translations.literal: Military supplies ordered late and not yet delivered—all are halted. Surplus grain levied in the first year—half is remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Military supplies still undelivered are cancelled; half the surplus grain levied in the first year is forgiven.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣軍戍並不得輒遣使民閒，務存優養。

translations.literal: Provinces, commanderies, counties, and garrison troops must not on their own dispatch envoys among the people; they shall strive to preserve generous care.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces, commanderies, counties, and garrisons must not send agents among the people without authorization; they shall treat the people with care.

sentences.zh: 若有侵擾，嚴為法制。

translations.literal: If there is harassment, the law shall be sternly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever harasses the people shall be punished under strict law."

sentences.zh: 」乙巳，輿駕親祠北郊。

translations.literal: " On yisi day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the emperor personally sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，振遠將軍、梁州刺史張立表稱去乙亥歲八月，[11]丹徒、蘭陵二縣界遺山側，一旦因濤水涌生，沙漲，周旋千餘頃，並膏腴，堪墾植。

translations.literal: On jiachen day, General Who Quells the Distance and Liangzhou Inspector Zhang Li memorialized that in the eighth month of the year before last, yihai, [11] on the flank of a remnant mountain at the border of Dantu and Lanling commanderies, all at once because of surging tide-waters sand piled up, circling more than a thousand qing, all fertile and fit for opening to cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Zhang Li, general who quells the distance and Liangzhou inspector, reported that in the eighth month two years before, [11] beside a remnant hill on the border of Dantu and Lanling, tidal flood had suddenly thrown up sand over a thousand qing of rich soil fit for cultivation.

sentences.zh: 戊午，輿駕親祠明堂。

translations.literal: On wuwu day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day the emperor personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 二月壬申，南豫州刺史沈泰奔于齊。

translations.literal: In the second month, on renshen day, South Yuzhou Inspector Shen Tai fled to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renshen day, Shen Tai, inspector of South Yuzhou, defected to Qi.

sentences.zh: [12]辛卯，詔車騎將軍、司空侯瑱總督水步眾軍以遏齊寇。

translations.literal: [12] On xinmao day an edict ordered Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of Works Hou Tian to take overall command of the water and land combined armies to check the Qi invaders.
translations.idiomatic: [12] On xinmao day an edict placed Hou Tian, grand general of chariots and cavalry and minister of works, in overall command of naval and land forces to block the Qi invasion.

sentences.zh: 三月甲午，詔曰：「罰不及嗣，自古通典，罪疑惟輕，布在方策。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiawu day, an edict said: "Punishment does not reach the sons—this is an ancient universal canon; when guilt is doubtful, lean toward leniency—it is set forth in the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu day, an edict declared: "Punishment does not fall on heirs—so the ancients taught; when guilt is in doubt, favor mercy—so the law books say."

sentences.zh: 沈泰反覆無行，遐邇所知，昔有微功，仍荷朝寄，剖符名郡，推轂累藩，漢口班師，還居方岳，良田有逾於四百，食客不止於三千，富貴顯榮，政當如此。

translations.literal: Shen Tai was fickle and without conduct, known far and near. In the past he had slight merit and still bore the court's trust; with divided tally he held a famed commandery, with chariot-shaft he was pushed up through many border posts. When the army withdrew from Hankou he returned to a territorial post. Good fields exceeded four hundred; retainers numbered no fewer than three thousand—wealth, honor, and glory ought indeed to be thus.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tai was treacherous and faithless, known throughout the realm. He had once done minor service and still held the court's trust; enfeoffed in a great commandery, promoted through many frontier posts. After the Hankou campaign he returned to provincial command. His estates ran to four hundred fields; his retainers to three thousand—such were the rewards of his rank."

sentences.zh: 鬼害其盈，天奪之魄，無故猖狂，自投獯醜。

translations.literal: Ghosts harmed his fullness; Heaven took his soul. Without cause he ran wild and threw himself among the savage foes.
translations.idiomatic: His pride invited ruin; Heaven withdrew his wits. Without provocation he rebelled and cast himself among the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 雖復知人則哲，惟帝其難，光武有蔽於龐萌，魏武不知於于禁，但令朝廷無我負人。

translations.literal: Though again to know men is wise and only the emperor finds it hard—Guangwu was blinded regarding Pang Meng; Weiwu did not know Yu Jin—only let the court have no case of Our failing others.
translations.idiomatic: Even the wise err in judging men—only an emperor finds it hardest. Guangwu was deceived by Pang Meng; Cao Cao misread Yu Jin. Let the court never say We wronged Our servants."

sentences.zh: 其部曲妻兒各令復業，所在及軍人若有恐脅侵掠者，皆以劫論。

translations.literal: His troops' wives and children are each ordered to resume their occupations. Wherever soldiers have intimidated or plundered, all are to be prosecuted as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers' families shall return to their trades. Any trooper who threatens or loots the people shall be punished as a brigand."

sentences.zh: 若有男女口為人所藏，並許詣臺申訴。

translations.literal: If any men or women are hidden by others, all are permitted to come to the capital to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone held in secret bondage may appeal at court."

sentences.zh: 若樂隨臨川王及節將立效者，悉皆聽許。

translations.literal: If any wish to follow the King of Linchuan and the commanders bearing staffs to render merit, all are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to serve the King of Linchuan or other commanders in earning merit may do so."

sentences.zh: 」乙卯，高祖幸後堂聽訟，還於橋上觀山水，賦詩示群臣。

translations.literal: " On yimao day the Founder visited the rear hall to hear lawsuits; returning, on the bridge he viewed mountains and waters and composed a poem to show the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the Founder heard cases in the rear hall; on his way back he paused on the bridge to take in the landscape and wrote a poem for his ministers.

sentences.zh: 是月，王琳立梁永嘉王蕭莊于郢州。

translations.literal: That month Wang Lin installed Liang's Prince of Yongjia, Xiao Zhuang, at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wang Lin set up Xiao Zhuang, Prince of Yongjia of Liang, at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，詔司空侯瑱、領軍將軍徐度率舟師為前軍，以討王琳。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi day, an edict ordered Minister of Works Hou Tian and Palace Bulwark General Xu Du to lead the fleet as the vanguard army to attack Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jisi day, an edict ordered Hou Tian, minister of works, and Xu Du, palace bulwark general, to lead the fleet as vanguard against Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊戌，輿駕幸石頭，親送填等。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the imperial carriage went to Stone City and personally sent off Tian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the emperor went to Stone City and personally saw off Hou Tian and the commanders.

sentences.zh: 己亥，江州刺史周迪擒王琳將李孝欽、樊猛、余孝頃于工塘。

translations.literal: On jihai day Jiangzhou Inspector Zhou Di captured Wang Lin's generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang at Gongtang.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day Zhou Di, inspector of Jiangzhou, took Wang Lin's generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang at Gongtang.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，遣吏部尚書謝哲諭王琳。

translations.literal: On jiachen day the Minister of Personnel Xie Zhe was sent to instruct Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Xie Zhe, minister of personnel, was dispatched to address Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，嘉禾一穗六岐生五城。

translations.literal: On jiayin day at Wucheng a single stalk of grain with six tines grew.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day a six-tined ear of grain appeared at Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 初，侯景之平也，火焚太極殿，承聖中議欲營之，獨闕一柱，至是有樟木大十八圍，長四丈五尺，流泊陶家後渚，監軍鄒子度以聞。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hou Jing was pacified, fire had burned the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate. In the Chengsheng era deliberation wished to rebuild it, but alone one pillar was lacking. Now there was a camphor tree eighteen arm-spans around and four zhang five chi long, drifting to moor at the rear ford of the Tao household. Supervising general Zou Zidu reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fell, fire had destroyed the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate. Under Emperor Chengsheng the court planned to rebuild it but lacked a single pillar. Now a camphor eighteen spans around and four zhang five chi long drifted to the Tao family's rear landing; the supervising general Zou Zidu reported it.

sentences.zh: 詔中書令沈眾兼起部尚書，少府卿蔡儔兼將作大匠，起太極殿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Central Secretariat Director Shen Zhong also to serve as Director of the Ministry that Raises Works, and Junior Chamberlain for the Palace Treasury Cai Chou also to serve as Director of Works, to raise the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Shen Zhong, director of the central secretariat, concurrent director of the ministry that raises works, and Cai Chou, junior chamberlain for the palace treasury, concurrent director of works, to rebuild the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 八月景寅，以廣梁郡為陳留郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yingyin day, Guangliang commandery was made Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yingyin day, Guangliang commandery was renamed Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔臨川王蒨西討，[13]以舟師五萬發自京師，輿駕幸冶城寺親送焉。

translations.literal: On xinwei day an edict ordered the King of Linchuan, Qian, on the western campaign; [13] with a fleet of fifty thousand he set out from the capital, and the imperial carriage went to Ye City Monastery to see him off in person.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day an edict sent the King of Linchuan, Qian, on the western campaign. [13] With fifty thousand sailors he sailed from the capital, and the emperor went in person to Ye City Monastery to see him off.

sentences.zh: 前開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史周文育，前鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史、新除開府儀同三司侯安都等於王琳所逃歸，自劾廷尉，即日引見，並宥之。

translations.literal: Former Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and South Yuzhou Inspector Zhou Wenyü, and former General Who Pacifies the North, South Xuzhou Inspector, and newly appointed Grand Mentor with Staff Hou Andu, who had escaped from Wang Lin's custody, impeached themselves before the Court for Punishments; that same day they were received in audience and all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyü, former grand mentor with staff and inspector of South Yuzhou, and Hou Andu, former general who pacifies the north, inspector of South Xuzhou, and newly made grand mentor with staff, who had escaped Wang Lin, presented themselves to the court of punishments to confess fault; that day they were received and pardoned.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔復文育等本官。

translations.literal: On wuyin day an edict restored Wenyü and the others to their former offices.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day an edict restored Wenyü and the others to their former posts.

sentences.zh: 壬午，追封皇子立為豫章王，諡曰獻；

translations.literal: On renwu day the Founder's son Li was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yuzhang, posthumous name Xian;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day the Founder's son Li was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yuzhang, posthumous name Xian;

sentences.zh: 權為長沙王，諡曰思；

translations.literal: Quan as King of Changsha, posthumous name Si;
translations.idiomatic: Quan as King of Changsha, posthumous name Si;

sentences.zh: 長女為永世公主，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: the eldest daughter as Princess of Eternal Generations, posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: and the eldest daughter as Princess of Eternal Generations, posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 謝哲反命，王琳請還鎮湘川，詔追眾軍緩其伐。

translations.literal: Xie Zhe returned with a contrary mandate. Wang Lin asked to return and hold Xiang River; an edict recalled the armies and suspended the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhe returned without agreement. Wang Lin asked to withdraw to the Xiang; an edict recalled the armies and halted the offensive.

sentences.zh: 癸未，西討眾軍至自大雷。

translations.literal: On guiwei day the western campaign armies arrived from Great Thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day the western expedition reached Great Thunder.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以信威將軍、江州刺史周迪為開府儀同三司，進號平南將軍。

translations.literal: On dinghai day the Trustworthy and Martial General and Jiangzhou Inspector Zhou Di was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Zhou Di, trustworthy and martial general and inspector of Jiangzhou, was made grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes and promoted to general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 改南徐州所領南蘭陵郡復為東海郡。

translations.literal: South Lanling commandery under South Xuzhou was again made Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: South Lanling commandery under South Xuzhou was restored as Donghai.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚午，遣鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司周文育都督眾軍出豫章，討余孝勱。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on gengwu day, Pacifying South General and Grand Mentor with Staff Zhou Wenyü was sent as commander-in-chief of the armies to march out of Yuzhang to attack Yu Xiaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on gengwu day, Zhou Wenyü, pacifying south general and grand mentor with staff, was sent from Yuzhang at the head of the armies against Yu Xiaoxiang.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，輿駕幸莊嚴寺，發金光明經題。

translations.literal: On yihai day the imperial carriage visited Zhuangyan Monastery and opened the lecture on the Sutra of Golden Light.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the emperor went to Zhuangyan Monastery to inaugurate the lecture on the Sutra of Golden Light.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以仁威將軍、高州刺史黃法𣰋為開府儀同三司，[14]進號鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: On dingyou day the Benevolent and Martial General and Gaozhou Inspector Huang Fa Tu was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes [14] and promoted to General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Huang Fa Tu, benevolent and martial general and inspector of Gaozhou, was made grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes [14] and promoted to general who guards the south.

sentences.zh: [15]甲寅，太極殿成，匠各給復。

translations.literal: [15] On jiayin day the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate was completed; each craftsman was given exemption from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: [15] On jiayin day the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate was finished; every craftsman was granted tax and labor exemption.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚申，侍中、安東將軍臨川王蒨率百僚朝前殿，拜上牛酒。

translations.literal: On gengshen day the Palace Attendant and Pacifying East General, the King of Linchuan Qian, led the hundred offices to the front hall of the palace to bow and present oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Qian, king of Linchuan, palace attendant and pacifying east general, led the hundred offices to the front hall to offer oxen and wine.

sentences.zh: 甲子，輿駕幸大莊嚴寺，設無遮大會，捨乘輿法物。

translations.literal: On jiazi day the imperial carriage visited the Great Zhuangyan Monastery and held an unbounded great assembly, donating the imperial carriage and ritual objects.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the emperor went to the Great Zhuangyan Monastery for a boundless great assembly and gave up the imperial carriage and ritual regalia.

sentences.zh: 群臣備法駕奉迎，即日輿駕還宮。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers with full ritual carriages came to welcome him; that same day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers with full ceremonial escort came to welcome him; that day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 景寅，高祖於太極殿東堂宴群臣，設金石之樂，以路寢告成也。

translations.literal: On yingyin day the Founder at the eastern hall of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate feasted the assembled ministers and set out metal and stone music, because the inner chamber dwelling was reported complete.
translations.idiomatic: On yingyin day the Founder feasted his ministers in the eastern hall of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate with full orchestra, celebrating completion of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 壬申，割吳郡鹽官、海鹽、前京三縣置海寧郡，屬揚州。

translations.literal: On renshen day from Wu commandery's Yanguan, Haiyan, and Qianjing counties Haining commandery was established, subordinate to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Haining commandery was carved from Yanguan, Haiyan, and Qianjing in Wu commandery and placed under Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以安成所部廣興六洞置安樂郡。

translations.literal: From Ancheng's six caves of Guangxing, Anle commandery was established.
translations.idiomatic: From the six caves of Guangxing in Ancheng, Anle commandery was established.

sentences.zh: 景戌，以寧遠將軍、北江州刺史熊曇朗為開府儀同三司，進號平西將軍。

translations.literal: On jingxu day the Pacifying Distance General and North Jiangzhou Inspector Xiong Tanlang was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: On jingxu day Xiong Tanlang, pacifying distance general and inspector of North Jiangzhou, was made grand mentor with staff and promoted to general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：「梁時舊仕，亂離播越，始還朝廷，多未銓序。

translations.literal: On dinghai day an edict said: "Former Liang officials, scattered by disorder, have only lately returned to court and for the most part have not yet been ranked.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict declared: "Former officials of Liang, scattered by the troubles, have only now returned to court and for the most part await appointment."

sentences.zh: 又起兵已來，軍勳甚眾。

translations.literal: Since the raising of armies, military merit has been very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Since the armies were raised, military merit has been abundant."

sentences.zh: 選曹即條文武簿及節將應九流者，量其所擬。

translations.literal: The Selection Office is immediately to list civil and military registers and commanders bearing staffs who fit the nine ranks, and weigh what posts suit them.
translations.idiomatic: The Selection Office shall at once compile rolls of civil and military men and of commanders with staffs eligible for the nine ranks, and assign posts as their talents warrant."

sentences.zh: 」於是隨材擢用者五十餘人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon more than fifty men were promoted according to ability.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty men were then promoted according to ability.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月己丑，青龍見于東方。

translations.literal: In the third year, first month, on jichou day, a green dragon appeared in the east.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, first month, on jichou day, a green dragon was seen in the east.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以鎮南將軍、廣州刺史歐陽頠即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On dingyou day the General Who Guards the South and Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei was given his present title as Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Ouyang Wei, general who guards the south and inspector of Guangzhou, was confirmed as grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 是夜大雪，及旦，太極殿前有龍跡見。

translations.literal: That night great snow fell, and at dawn dragon tracks were seen before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: That night heavy snow fell; by dawn dragon tracks appeared before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 甲午，廣州刺史歐陽頠表稱白龍見于州江南岸，[16]長數十丈，大可八九圍，歷州城西道入天井崗。

translations.literal: On jiawu day Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei memorialized that a white dragon appeared on the south bank south of the province, [16] several tens of zhang long and eight or nine arm-spans around, passing west along the provincial city road into Heavenly Well Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Ouyang Wei, inspector of Guangzhou, reported a white dragon on the south bank south of the city, [16] tens of zhang in length and eight or nine spans around, which passed west along the city road into Heavenly Well Ridge.

sentences.zh: 仙人見于羅浮山寺小石樓，長三丈所，通身潔白，衣服楚麗。

translations.literal: An immortal appeared at the small stone tower of Luofu Mountain Monastery, about three zhang tall, all body pure white, garments splendid in Chu style.
translations.idiomatic: An immortal was seen at the small stone tower on Luofu Mountain, some three zhang tall, wholly white, dressed in splendid Chu fashion.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，詔曰：「南康、始興王諸妹，已有封爵，依禮止是藩主。

translations.literal: On xinchou day an edict said: "The younger sisters of the kings of Nankang and Shixing already have enfeoffments; by ritual they should only be feudal ladies.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day an edict declared: "The younger sisters of the kings of Nankang and Shixing already hold titles; by ritual they should rank only as feudal princesses."

sentences.zh: 此二王者，有殊恆情，宜隆禮數。

translations.literal: These two kings have a special constant feeling; ritual measure ought to be exalted.
translations.idiomatic: These two kings stand in a special bond; their sisters deserve higher honor."

sentences.zh: 諸主儀秩及尚主，可並同皇女。

translations.literal: The princesses' ritual ranks and those who marry them may both be the same as imperial daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Let the princesses' ceremonial standing and their husbands' ranks equal those of the emperor's own daughters."

sentences.zh: 」戊申，詔臨川王蒨省揚、徐二州辭訟。

translations.literal: " On wushen day an edict ordered the King of Linchuan, Qian, to review lawsuits of Yang and Xu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day an edict charged the King of Linchuan, Qian, with hearing appeals from Yang and Xu provinces.

sentences.zh: 二月辛酉，以平西將軍、桂州刺史淳于量為開府儀同三司，進號鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinyou day, the General Who Pacifies the West and Guizhou Inspector Chunyu Liang was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to Grand General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinyou day, Chunyu Liang, general who pacifies the west and inspector of Guizhou, was made grand mentor with staff and promoted to grand general who guards the west.

sentences.zh: 壬午，司空侯瑱督眾軍自江入合州，焚齊舟艦。

translations.literal: On renwu day Minister of Works Hou Tian commanded the armies from the river into Hefei and burned Qi's boats.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Hou Tian, minister of works, led the armies from the Yangtze into Hefei and burned Qi's fleet.

sentences.zh: 三月景申，侯瑱至自合肥，眾軍獻捷。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jingshen day, Hou Tian returned from Hefei; the armies presented the spoils.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jingshen day, Hou Tian returned from Hefei and the armies reported victory.

sentences.zh: 夏閏四月庚寅，詔曰：「開廩賑絕，育民之大惠，巡方恤患，前王之令典。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of summer, on gengyin day, an edict said: "Opening granaries to relieve the destitute is the great bounty for nurturing the people; touring the regions to pity the afflicted is the former kings' established canon.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of summer, on gengyin day, an edict declared: "Opening the granaries to save the starving is the great act of nurturing the people; touring the realm to ease suffering is the ancient kings' law."

sentences.zh: 朕當斯季俗，膺此樂推，君德未孚，民瘼猶甚，重茲多壘，彌疚納隍。

translations.literal: We meet this declining age and receive this joyful succession; Our lordly virtue is not yet trusted, the people's afflictions are still severe. Heaping ramparts upon ramparts, We are the more ashamed to stand at the brink.
translations.idiomatic: "We came to power in a fallen age and accepted the people's acclaim, yet Our virtue has not won their hearts and their suffering remains deep. Fortress upon fortress of trouble fills Us with shame."

sentences.zh: 良由四聰弗達，[17]千里勿應。

translations.literal: Truly because the four keen listeners were not reached, [17] a thousand li gave no response.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the four keen listeners were not heard, [17] and no voice answered from a thousand li."

sentences.zh: [18]博施之仁，何其或爽？

translations.literal: [18] The benevolence of broad giving—how could it ever fail?
translations.idiomatic: [18] How could the grace of broad giving ever be wanting?"

sentences.zh: 殘弊之軌，致此未康。

translations.literal: The track of ruin and exhaustion brought this not yet to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the road of ruin and exhaustion has not yet led to peace."

sentences.zh: 吳州、縉州去歲蝗旱，郢田雖呪，[19]鄭渠終涸，室靡盈積之望，家有填壑之嗟。

translations.literal: Wu and Jing provinces last year suffered locusts and drought. Though the fields of Ying were charmed, [19] the Zheng Canal in the end dried up. Houses had no hope of full stores; families had the lament of filling gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Jing provinces suffered locusts and drought last year. Though the fields of Ying were blessed, [19] the Zheng Canal ran dry at last. No household could hope for a full granary; many faced starvation."

sentences.zh: 百姓不足，兆民何賴？

translations.literal: If the hundred surnames are not sufficient, on what do the myriad people rely?
translations.idiomatic: When the people lack food, what can the realm depend upon?"

sentences.zh: 近已遣中書舍人江德藻銜命東陽，與令長二千石問民疾苦，仍以入臺倉見米分恤。

translations.literal: Recently We have sent Palace Attendant Jiang Dezao bearing Our mandate to Dongyang to question the people and officials of two thousand piculs rank about their hardships, and likewise to divide and comfort them with rice from the capital granary on hand.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately sent Jiang Dezao, palace attendant, to Dongyang with Our mandate to inquire into the people's hardships with the local magistrates, and to distribute grain from the capital granaries in relief."

sentences.zh: 雖德非既飽，庶微慰阻飢。

translations.literal: Though Our virtue is not yet that of full satiety, We hope in small measure to comfort those who block hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Our virtue is not yet enough to fill every belly, yet We hope in some measure to ease those who starve."

sentences.zh: 」甲午，詔依前代置西省學士，兼以伎術者預焉。

translations.literal: " On jiawu day an edict ordered, following former dynasties, Western Secretariat scholars established, and moreover those skilled in arts and techniques to be included.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day an edict, following earlier dynasties, established scholars of the Western Secretariat, including men skilled in arts and techniques.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，遣鎮北將軍徐度率眾城南皖口。

translations.literal: On dingyou day Pacifying North General Xu Du led the armies south to Wan Estuary.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Xu Du, pacifying north general, led the armies south to Wan Estuary.

sentences.zh: 是時久不雨，景午，輿駕幸鍾山祠蔣帝廟，是日降雨，迄于月晦。

translations.literal: At this time rain had long been lacking. On jingwu day the imperial carriage visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang; that day rain fell, continuing until the month's end.
translations.idiomatic: Rain had long been absent. On jingwu day the emperor sacrificed at Emperor Jiang's temple on Zhongshan; rain fell that day and lasted to month's end.

sentences.zh: 五月景辰朔，日有食之，有司奏：舊儀，御前殿，服朱紗袍、通天冠。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, jingchen, there was a solar eclipse. The relevant offices memorialized: According to old ritual, at the front hall one wears the vermilion gauze robe and the penetrating-heaven crown.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month, jingchen, there was a solar eclipse. The relevant offices reported the old rite: at the front hall the emperor should wear the vermilion gauze robe and penetrating-heaven crown.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「此乃前代承用，意有未同。

translations.literal: An edict said: "This is what former generations used in succession; the intent is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Former generations followed this practice, but the meaning is not the same."

sentences.zh: 合朔仰助太陽，宜備袞冕之服。

translations.literal: At the conjunction one looks up to aid the sun; one ought to prepare the robes of the full regalia.
translations.idiomatic: At the conjunction one assists the sun; full imperial regalia should be worn."

sentences.zh: 自今已去，永可為准。

translations.literal: From now onward this shall forever be the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth this shall be the permanent rule."

sentences.zh: 」景寅，扶南國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: " On yingyin day Funan sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On yingyin day Funan sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，北江州刺史熊曇朗殺都督周文育于軍，舉兵反。

translations.literal: On yiyou day North Jiangzhou Inspector Xiong Tanlang killed Commander-in-Chief Zhou Wenyü in the army and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day Xiong Tanlang, inspector of North Jiangzhou, murdered the commander Zhou Wenyü in camp and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 王琳遣其將常眾愛、曹慶率兵援余孝勱。

translations.literal: Wang Lin sent his generals Chang Zhong'ai and Cao Qing leading troops to aid Yu Xiaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent his generals Chang Zhong'ai and Cao Qing with troops to support Yu Xiaoxiang.

sentences.zh: 六月戊子，儀同侯安都敗眾愛等於左里，獲琳從弟襲、主帥羊暕等三十餘人，眾愛遁走，庚寅，廬山民斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Hou Andu defeated Zhong'ai and the others at Zuoli, capturing Wang Lin's younger cousin Xi, chief commander Yang Xian, and more than thirty others. Zhong'ai fled; on gengyin day the people of Lushan beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Hou Andu, bearer of staff equal to the three dukes, routed Zhong'ai at Zuoli and took Wang Lin's cousin Xi, the commander Yang Xian, and more than thirty others. Zhong'ai fled; on gengyin day the people of Lushan killed him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲午，眾師凱歸。

translations.literal: On jiawu day the armies returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day the armies returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「曇朗噬逆，罪不容誅，分命眾軍，仍事掩討，方加梟磔，以明刑憲。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Tanlang devoured and rebelled; his crime brooks no execution. We ordered the armies to continue the concealed attack; when he is exposed to the halter and cleaver, the penal statutes will be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Tanlang has turned traitor and murderer; his crime admits no pardon. The armies are already hunting him; when he is taken, the law will be made plain."

sentences.zh: 」徵臨川王蒨往皖口置城柵，以錢道戢守焉。

translations.literal: " The King of Linchuan, Qian, was summoned to Wan Estuary to set up stockades and palisades; Qian Daozai was left to defend them.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Linchuan, Qian, was called to Wan Estuary to build fortifications, with Qian Daozai left to hold them.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，高祖不豫，遣兼太宰、尚書左僕射王通以疾告太廟，兼太宰、中書令謝哲告大社、南北郊。

translations.literal: On dingyou day the Founder was unwell. He sent Concurrent Grand Minister of Sacrifices and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Tong to report the illness to the Grand Temple, and Concurrent Grand Minister of Sacrifices and Central Secretariat Director Xie Zhe to report to the Grand Altar and the southern and northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the Founder fell ill. He sent Wang Tong, concurrent grand minister of sacrifices and left vice director of the secretariat, to announce his illness at the Grand Temple, and Xie Zhe, concurrent grand minister of sacrifices and director of the central secretariat, to announce it at the Grand Altar and the suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，高祖疾小瘳。

translations.literal: On xinchou day the Founder's illness slightly improved.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day the Founder's illness eased slightly.

sentences.zh: 故司空周文育之柩至自建昌。

translations.literal: The coffin of the late Minister of Works Zhou Wenyü arrived from Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: The coffin of the late Zhou Wenyü, minister of works, arrived from Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，高祖素服哭于東堂，哀甚。

translations.literal: On renyin day the Founder in plain robes wept in the eastern hall, grief extreme.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day the Founder, in plain mourning dress, wept in the eastern hall with deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，高祖臨訊獄

translations.literal: On guimao day the Founder personally inspected and questioned at the pris
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day the Founder personally heard prison cases.

translations.literal: (omitted)
translations.idiomatic: (omitted)
