translations.idiomatic: ons.

sentences.zh: [20]是夜，熒惑在天尊。

translations.literal: [20] That night the Sparkling Deluder was at the Celestial Honored One.
translations.idiomatic: [20] That night Mars stood at the Celestial Honored One.

sentences.zh: 高祖疾又甚。

translations.literal: The Founder's illness again grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder's illness worsened again.

sentences.zh: [21]景午，崩于璿璣殿，時年五十七。

translations.literal: [21] On jingwu day he died at the Hall of the Rotating Pearl, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: [21] On jingwu day he died in the Hall of the Rotating Pearl, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 遺詔追臨川王蒨入纂。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict recalled the King of Linchuan, Qian, to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His testament summoned the King of Linchuan, Qian, to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大行皇帝遷殯于太極殿西階。

translations.literal: On jiayin day the late emperor's coffin was moved to lie in state at the western steps of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the late emperor's coffin was placed in state at the western steps of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 秋八月甲午，群臣上諡曰武皇帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, the assembled ministers posthumously titled him Emperor Wu, temple name Founder.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, the ministers gave him the posthumous title Emperor Wu and the temple name Founder.

sentences.zh: 景申，葬萬安陵。

translations.literal: On jingshen day he was buried at Wan'an Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On jingshen day he was buried at Wan'an Tomb.

sentences.zh: 高祖智以綏物，武以寧亂，英謀獨運，人皆莫及，故能征伐四克，靜難夷凶。

translations.literal: The Founder with wisdom pacified things, with martial prowess settled disorder; his heroic stratagem worked alone—none could match him. Therefore he could conquer on campaign in four directions and quiet hardship and level the fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder pacified the realm through wisdom and quelled chaos through arms; his strategy was his alone, and none could rival it. Thus he conquered in every direction and stilled rebellion and slaughter.

sentences.zh: 至升大麓之日，居阿衡之任，恆崇寬政，愛育為本。

translations.literal: When he ascended the great footstool's day he occupied the office of Aheng; he constantly honored lenient government and took cherishing nurture as the root.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne he held the burden of chief minister to the realm; he always favored lenient rule and made cherishing the people his foundation.

sentences.zh: 有須發調軍儲，皆出於事不可息。

translations.literal: Whenever it was necessary to issue levies for army stores, all arose from affairs that could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he levied grain for the armies, it was only because necessity would not allow rest.

sentences.zh: 加以儉素自率，常膳不過數品，私饗曲宴，皆瓦器蚌盤，肴核庶羞，裁令充足而已，不為虛費。

translations.literal: Moreover he led by frugal simplicity himself; ordinary meals were no more than a few dishes. Private feasts and informal banquets all used earthenware and clam shells for dishes; meat and vegetables were only enough to suffice—not for empty waste.
translations.idiomatic: He was frugal in his own habits: daily meals were only a few courses; private feasts used pottery and clam shells, with food no more than enough—never spent on display.

sentences.zh: 初平侯景，及立紹泰，子女玉帛，皆班將士。

translations.literal: When he first pacified Hou Jing, and when he established Shaotai, children, jade, and silks were all distributed to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: After he first subdued Hou Jing and again when he set up the Shaotai regime, sons and daughters, jade, and silks were all shared out among his officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其充闈房者，衣不重綵，飾無金翠，哥鍾女樂，不列於前。

translations.literal: Those who filled the inner quarters wore no double brocade; ornaments had no gold or kingfisher; song-bells and female musicians were not arrayed before him.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the inner quarters wore no doubled brocade; ornaments bore no gold or kingfisher feather; bells and female musicians were not set before him.

sentences.zh: 及乎踐祚，彌厲恭儉。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he was even stricter in respectful frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne, he was stricter still in modest frugality.

sentences.zh: 故隆功茂德，光有天下焉。

translations.literal: Therefore his lofty merit and abundant virtue shone over all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thus his towering merit and rich virtue held sway over the realm.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：高祖英略大度，應變無方，蓋漢高、魏武之亞矣。

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: The Founder's heroic strategy was broad and magnanimous; in meeting change he had no fixed method—he was next only to Han Gaozu and Wei Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: The Founder's genius was vast and his bearing magnanimous; he met every turn without a set plan—only Han Gaozu and Cao Cao could stand beside him.

sentences.zh: 及西都盪覆，誠貫天人。

translations.literal: When the western capital was overthrown, his sincerity pierced Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: When the western capital fell, his loyalty ran through Heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯闕伊尹之才，空結桐宮之憤，貞陽假秦兵之送，不思穆嬴之泣。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian lacked Yiyin's talent yet vainly nursed the grievance of the Tung Palace; Zhenyang borrowed the escort of Qin troops yet did not think of Mu Ying's weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian lacked the gift of an Yiyin yet brooded on the wrong of the Tung Palace; Zhenyang leaned on northern troops yet never remembered Mu Ying's tears.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃蹈玄機而撫末運，乘勢隙而拯橫流，王跡所基，始自於此，何至戡黎升陑之捷而已焉。

translations.literal: The Founder then trod the dark mystery to comfort the declining age, seized the gap in the tide to rescue the crosscurrent—the royal foundations began here; how could it be only the victory of defeating the Li people and ascending Yang?
translations.idiomatic: The Founder then walked the hidden Way to steady a dying age, caught the breach in the flood to save the realm—the throne's roots began here; it was far more than the triumph at Li and the ascent of Mount Yang.

sentences.zh: 故於慎徽時序之世，變聲改物之辰，兆庶歸以謳歌，炎靈去如釋負，方之前代，何其美乎！

translations.literal: Therefore in the age of careful compliance with the seasons and proper sequence, at the time of changing sounds and altering things, the myriad people returned in song; the blazing spirit departed as if a burden were lifted—compared with former ages, how beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: In that age of careful ritual and renewed order, when music and customs were remade, the people sang him home and the old mandate slipped away like a load set down—set beside earlier dynasties, how fine a founding it was!

translations.idiomatic: On "your subject Baxian": the text originally read "taboo name," preserving Yao Cha's wording; as a Liang and Chen historian he avoided the imperial name.

translations.idiomatic: The same applies below.

translations.idiomatic: Defender means commandery governor; the phrase means a governor enfeoffed by tally.

translations.idiomatic: The collator did not recognize Chang Yizhi as a personal name, added a mouth radical to chang, and inserted chu—a blunder worth laughing at."

sentences.zh: 良由四聰弗達 「達」原訛「遠」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Truly because the four acute ears did not reach: "reach" was originally corrupted to "far"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "the four acute ears did not reach": the text originally read far for reach; other editions are correct; emended.

sentences.zh: 千里勿應 「勿」原訛「功」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: A thousand li did not respond: "did not" was originally corrupted to "merit"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "a thousand li did not respond": the text originally read merit for did not; other editions are correct; emended.

sentences.zh: 郢田雖呪 「呪」北監本、汲本、殿本作「疏」。

translations.literal: Though the fields of Ying were prayed over: "prayed"—the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions read "thinned."
translations.idiomatic: On "though the fields of Ying were prayed over": the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions read thinned.

sentences.zh: 按呪通祝。

translations.literal: Comment—zhu passes for zhu (to pray).
translations.idiomatic: Note: zhu here equals the word for prayer.

sentences.zh: 謂此用《史記·淳于髡傳》穰田之文，應作「呪」。

translations.literal: holds that this uses the passage on praying for the millet fields in the Biography of Chunyu Kun in the Records of the Grand Historian, and it should read "prayed."
translations.idiomatic: argues that the line echoes the millet-field prayer in the Biography of Chunyu Kun (Records of the Grand Historian) and should read prayed.

sentences.zh: 高祖疾又甚 按北監本、汲本、殿本無「又」字。

translations.idiomatic: On "the Founder's illness again grew severe": the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions omit again.
